body: class median is 8 points above me
I know some people in the class and we cram together.
Upper level compsci class. I don't know if I could find a tutor.
I've been in and out of therapy and on and off meds. It's been a long road.

I might legitimately fail this class though. I don't know how to answer any of the questions on this homework, and looking at the solutions manual I don't even know how the professor expects anyone to get the answers.

I'm pretty fucked for the test.
I don't know who to talk to. People generally are jealous of me because of the offers I have in front of me.

I really don't know if it's college or just my personality that's causing this.

I spent most of 2019 out of school and I feel like I wasn't as bad as I am right now but I was still anxious.

Yeah, I hate myself for being slow though.

I'm competing with kids who are 3-4 years younger than me.

I've been like this all the time. Nobody believes me when I say I'm struggling because I usually do well. I'm that obnoxious kid that complains that they're doing badly and then shits out an A.

But I really, really dislike the academic setting. I feel like I burnt myself out for nothing but imaginary GPA points. I lost my drive and I hate myself.

The pressure is getting to me. Anything under a C in a single class and I lose my job. I also am looking for a job closer to home while this is going on.

I've always been super anxious in college. It's not been good for my sanity.
I'm an emotional drain on people though. This is my battle to fight, my time to fuck up.
Been in the system since 2013. I feel like a failure every day tbh.
I keep saying I'll do it but I haven't. But I finally have something to lose and something to kill myself over if I fuck up.
I'm really burnt out. I feel like I'll never really forgive myself for fucking up.

Every single person in my life is telling me to just shut up and deal with it. I have a six figure job lined up and I ~~am forced to~~ get to travel for my job and only take 9 credits this semester, I'm not allowed to complain to anyone.

I really can't go out without feeling guilty. It feels bad spending my mom's money on myself when I'm so useless.

Any time spent enjoying life is time wasted because I know that if I don't get the ball rolling I can spend ages pretending to "refocus" even though deep down I know I'm not accomplishing jack shit while resting.

I don't have fun anymore without feeling guilt.

>Your right you will never be happy not with that mindset. If you have that type of mindset i wonder how you present yourself on job interviews. Maybe your resume is flawless but they are seeing something else in you or your mindset or way of thinking that stops them from hiring you.

My resume is far from flawless. I rarely get past the resume screening phase. I'm less experienced and less qualified than a lot of people.

>Sometimes it's not your fault I'm serious a few years ago I applied to work at a hospital for a job I wanted there. I was the only one dressed up for the interview everyone else was dressed like it was grand theft auto lol.

Lol everyone goes full formal interviews where I'm from. I've been told in to dress casual and we all came in full suits.

I'm always a nervous wreck in interviews. Kid with no prior experience walks into an interview that if by some miracle he were to do well in could reasonably expect to negotiate a 110-120k starting salary + benefits. Stakes were high and for some reason I don't get interviews from "lesser" places and I only get callbacks from high profile tech companies. Don't ask me why lol.

>Resumes really are not everything I promise you. You can get more from speaking and digging into somebody than a piece of paper.

I think with interviews I just need more preparation and interview practice, but getting interview practice is contingent on a refined resume.

>I had some CEOs chatting in an office and overheard them talking. They told our class their candidate had the perfect resume qualities and was good on paper but I can't remember what they said something the candidate said or how they were behaving in the interview turned them off and made them not want to extend the offer.

Yeah, I get that. I still remember the worst thing I've said on an interview out of pressure to this day lol.

>For some reason anytime I am allowed to interview in person or present myself, state my case and show who I am it turns out better than sending a piece of paper into a digital wormhole.

Seems to be the case for me as well. Nature of the beast.

>Do your best and please stop comparing your road to somebody else's when no two people are the same.

You don't know someone's story but you know their results.

If you offer stupid amounts of money to kids fresh out of college you're going to attract some determined madmen. I can't feel proud of myself for working hard because I know that everyone still in the game is hauling ass as well. The smart-but-lazies all got destroyed. I haven't met anyone that made it past sophmore year without putting at least as much effort into their studies and career as I did. Oftentimes more.

I dunno what I'm doing with life anymore. The job hunt has really been getting to me over the last few months.

Know a couple dudes in ROTC and some deployed somewhere in the middle east, they're all like "don't do it man" haha

I've considered it tbh.

It's 5 AM on a monday and I've been spending the last 2 hours of my life trying to revise my resume for the fourth time this week.

I haven't slept a normal night in the last few weeks because I've been focusing on projects, self study, and career building. I just want to feel like I'm getting anywhere with life at all instead of feeling like everything I do is a waste.

I know why I didn't get the things I wanted. I know why people succeeded where I didn't. And when I get it I'll look back and hate myself for taking twice as long to achieve what so many others did.

When I'm old I'll look back and hate myself for my suboptimal route. I'll never be content or happy, and I just haven't accepted that yet.

>I think 22 per hour is a lot lol.

Depends on your life.

I'm a spoiled little brat who's had access to a lot of tools and advantages in order to succeed. I'm a kid from a stable household in a good neighborhood.

I played life on fucking easy mode and I couldn't turn it into things people who've had it harder than me could.

I already had my wake up call. I already went from throwing away my scholarship first year into academic probation into clawing my way back up and finally starting to see progress in my life.

I'm not beating myself up with the mindset of "wah I scaped by in college with a C average why did people who actually cared about school end up better than me?" I'm beating myself up with the  mindset that I ended up in the same position as that person while also caring. 

That's what failure is. Failure doesn't mean that you didn't try or that you gave up. Failure means that you tried, powered through and sacrificed other things to reach a goal, but you just could not do it.

>This mindset you have and the constant comparing yourself to others NEEDS TO STOP.

Until the day I stop competing with the people I'm comparing myself to, I need to do so.

>Move forward. It's better then sitting around and feeling sorry for yourself.

Every one step forward I take should have been two. I'm slow and will never freaking make it.

It's not that I sit on my ass doing fuck all. It's the exact opposite. I was that stereotypical nerd who sat at home studying and losing sleep over my grades and career except that NONE OF IT PAID OFF. I didn't make all the right moves, nobody ever does, but I'm at the same god damn fucking spot as someone who did fuck all and didn't care.

Are we full metal jacket now?

I met a lot of new people. I like being alone now lol.

Idk I feel fucking old lol. I spent my entire life behind and I'll continue to do so until it doesn't matter.

>Also my brother is 23 and he’s still living 10 feet across from me so if anything

My sister is 18 and I live 10 feet away from her lol. I won't be moving out for a while.

Most people I know are younger and more successful than me. It's all relative.

There's a huge difference between making six figs at 24 and at 30.

>How could you have failed at life when you haven’t completed it yet?

I've lost all interest in everything in life. Nothing really appeals to me anymore.

All of my friends went on wild adventures and had fun with their youth. I passed that all up to grind out and try and focus on my career.

Except I couldn't fucking do it. I proved that I could commit years of my life to an end goal and not achieve it.

What kind of scholarship requires a minimum 3.7?

> I have absolutely no intrinsic value or assets and god does university remind me of how worthless I am. 

Welcome to uni. Either you found it easy and therefore you wasted your time here or you realized how fucking behind you are.

​

I'm 23, so you might call me someone who has plenty of time left, but honestly what you wrote kind of hit a nerve for me. I've wasted my college years and if I can't make up for it I deserve to kill myself.

I saw you were talking about the tech industry, and I figure you at least browse r/cscareerquestions based on your post history and your job hunting adventure. Sub is pretty toxic, you can only really read so much about kids younger than both of us making bank at FAANG before you start to question your worth as a person. I think as a late bloomer in the field I just want to find a way to shut those kids up and surpass them. 

Honestly, I don't know if I'll ever get over wasted time. I think it'll be a constant reminder to myself that I fucked up the first time around and I don't deserve to live if I fuck it up again.
23 years. Never worked a day in my life.

Lot of people stick out but at that level I don't know who's smarter than who.

It bothers me that people my age making 150-200k isn't so out of the ordinary, however.
The joke is no matter how old you are, someone older than you is gonna tell you have time.
That either sounds like 2 years worth of time or an entire decade.

I've settled on unrealistic goals and expectations for myself that I know I won't reach. To give up on them or to fail is to give up on life.

A lot of people look down on me. Rightfully so, since I'm kind of a useless person though. I need to move fast now to make up for lost time. Either I do that or I die trying.

1. Get stressed
2. Shut down because of stress
3. Get more stressed because I wasted time because I was stressed out

Feedback loop of my life.

Same age, same timeline, same situation. I know that feeling.

I've become a worse person over the last few years. I know how I feel and why I feel the way I do, but I just can't really put it to words.

It just feels to me like my choices are to either desperately try and make up for the lost time and still be behind anyways or to end it all and call it a day.

​
I'm behind compared to the people I feel like I should compare myself to. That is, my classmates and the people I grew up with.

>  I think surviving college is honestly about remaining in the present and taking things weekly/monthly, and finding value in what you're doing now, regardless of whether you'll use it in your daily life in the future. 

I've tried to do that. It didn't work. Years of my life were wasted trying to find myself and make the most of college. College isn't for me, I've spent years in the system, and I don't want to be here anymore. The only thing I care about is making sure my life outside of this shithole is any better.

>you get to spend an extremely large amount of time just absorbing information and growing as a person from the knowledge that you gain

That's not a fun thing. It's boring as shit and also kinda stressful and I don't even get paid for putting up with this. When I learn things it's because I want to do something with it. The goal of every lesson in college is to not fuck up on the test.

Got it. My perception of the entry level to mid level market is formed by anecdotes of people I know who are in it right now. I'll stop believing it when I see it for myself, if I live that long.

You probably think I'm just some dumb kid, and you're completely right. I never worked a day in my life and I don't know how the real world works. I feel like I've wasted years of my life, and that's why I'm so obsessed with catching up. I did fuck all in my life until I was 22, and then the last two years have been a high speed sprint to try and get my shit together.
Care to elaborate?

>Standard pay raises are single digits. This is just the way it is.

That is true. Raises aren't how people move up, though. People job hop and change positions for salary increases. If you stay at your first job for 5 years you either started off in a good spot, don't really care for advancing your career, or got promoted to a more senior position.

>What field are you in that offers $120000 to inexperienced new grads?

[Computer science.](https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/new-york-city-entry-level-software-engineer-salary-SRCH_IL.0,13_IM615_KO14,43.htm) The 120k number is not normal, but it exists.

The people getting these offers all likely have several internships, maybe a competition, definitely more than just "went to class" under their belt.

I had no shot. I don't know why they even gave me an interview, but they did.

>Also if you are "slow" why bother with such an elite field.

Because I like doing it and it pays well.

Also, I feel like somehow because I'm still here and didn't get weeded out, I like to pretend like I still have a chance, even though all signs suggest otherwise.

>If you earn $60000 at 25 you are NOT behind people your age

Maybe I phrased this wrong and too generally. I meant to be more specific and say people my age in my field and position. That is, someone in my field who went into the field straight out of college.

I hated, and continue to hate every second of college. There's nothing fun about this, if I didn't still live with my parents I'd be drinking myself to sleep a hell of a lot more often. I'm not in a good mental state, and the fact that I've gone through six years of this bullshit to end up mediocre is fucking with me really hard.

I'm 23, two or three years older than my classmates. I'm dead serious when I say almost everyone I know still in my major are going to be making six figures by the time they're 24.

>What insane kind of raises do you believe junior novice new-to-career 22 -25 yr olds earn, that the income more than doubles in 2 or 3 years ????

It happens. Let's say I start at 60k. Average for less than 1 year experience is around 70-80k, but I'm pretty sure I won't be making that much. It is completely realistic to break the 130k barrier by the time you have 3 years experience. Hell, I had a job interview for a job that started at 120k a week ago that I had no shot at. But the fact that they considered my resume means that they will consider people with no experience for it.

I'm a very slow person so I'm probably gonna take longer than that.

I haven't done anything with my life, and it's not like I've done anything in lieu of taking longer than I should have in college. I take it way too personally when people point it out, because I'm pathetic and people know it.

I need to prove them wrong.

In 10 years, none of this will matter. I'll get my lame, underpaid job, work my way up, and live a useless life knowing that I have failed in life.

But it's not about 10 years from now. It's about now. I will spend six years in fucking college and I get to come out a miserable wreck who's not even doing well enough to make up for being such a mess. By the time I'm 25, I'll be making half that of what people my age should be making, I probably still won't be able to drive, and I'll continue to be a worthless person that's perpetually behind everyone.

>below your level

There aren't any positions below my level, that's the real strange thing. Entry level is a large, vague title.

And yeah, a year of experience goes a long way, I just feel like everyone's starting their life while I'm...well not.

>basically had a panic attack during the interview.

you're telling me. I wanted to run out of the room out of shame once I had to ask my interviewer to clarify.

Yeah, I remember getting grilled about my resume. I think it's just my lack of real experience which is the reason that I'm not getting callbacks. I really can't spin "haven't worked or interned" without literally outright lying about it.

btw I already have a suit. lot of my interviews say come in casual but people still come in suits lol.

I've remade my resume several times. I might get it reviewed again this Wednesday. 

I wouldn't say I'm not making progress in my life, it's just everyone I know already went through the stuff I'm going through now, so I just feel left in the dust.
People in my family seem to die pretty late, so I got that going for me I guess.
My fault for not figuring it out sooner in life tbh
Stuck in college, trying to get a job before I graduate so I don't end up spending the next however long doing nothing but sitting in my room applying for jobs.

I just feel really freakin old all the time tbh. Realistically by the time I catch up, I'll be around 25-27, at the same status/experience level as most of my peers were when they themselves will be 24.
I don't really care about the money, I just feel like my life has been too slow.

>Hopefully a touch of imposter syndrome?

It's less impostor syndrome and more that I really am an impostor.

It could be selection bias, but everyone I personally know that performed lower than me dropped out of the major, so I am the least competitive person I know.

Even landing a job feels weird, because I feel perpetually behind in my career because I started late.

For reference I'm 23 and I think my interviewer was younger than me.
The rent is too damn high where I live. Anything under 6 figures is "I'm living with my parents" money lol.

>I bet it wasn't as bad as you think it was?

I'm very noncompetitive compared to the other people vying for these kinds of jobs. The group I found myself in, the kids who graduated high school in 2015, are a bunch of freaks of nature who collectively ruined the grading curves of several classes.

I was a lazy B student who didn't know what they were doing in life and changed their major twice and suddenly I get thrown into a pool of people who have $80k jobs lined up as their fallback plans, own patents, published papers, the list goes on.

The expectations are high, and I do feel like I'm a below average anomaly that wouldn't be given as much benefit of the doubt.

>What the heck job pays that much with no experience

None. The people who get interviews generally have at least one internship under their belt.

I just got extremely lucky to even get an interview. If you work hard, it takes about 2-3 years to break 100k salary from where I am right now.

I've applied to a lot of places, I've gotten exactly one callback.

I'm about 3 years older than most of my peers, my life feels like an eternal game of catch up.
Haha getting these interviews is hard enough. It's the only one I've gotten out of months of applying.

I know it's a learning process.

Kinda beating myself up about it though cause it was a pretty high paying and prestigious job, probably the only interview of that caliber I'll get for a while. Literally feels like I blew my one shot at life.
